note: Protein per 100 g as eaten unless marked DRY.

items.name: Soya chunks
items.how: Cheapest protein per rupee in Pakistan. Soak 30 min, squeeze, bhuno in salan like meat.
items.caution: Start with small portions if you are not used to them.

items.name: Bhuna chana (roasted)
items.how: The famous shake is real: grind with milk and dates. Or eat dry as a snack.
items.caution: About 60 g carbs per 100 g - count the kcal.

items.name: Sattu
items.how: 2-3 tbsp with water or milk and a pinch of salt or jaggery - the classic desi shake.

items.name: Boiled chana
items.how: Chana chaat with onion, tomato and lemon - protein plus volume for pennies.

items.name: Daal (masoor / moong)
items.how: Daal with roti or rice together form a complete protein. Cooked is about 9 g per 100 g.

items.name: Lobia
items.how: Lobia ka salan - cheap and filling.

items.name: Eggs
items.how: The cheapest complete protein: 3-4 eggs give 20-26 g. About 6-7 g per egg.

items.name: Dahi
items.how: Strain in a cloth for hung curd - protein nearly doubles per 100 g.

items.name: Moongphali (peanuts)
items.how: Real protein, but very calorie-dense. A fistful, not a bag.
items.caution: 567 kcal per 100 g - easy to overeat.

items.name: Kaleji (chicken liver)
items.how: Iron and protein at a throwaway price.
items.caution: Very high in vitamin A - a couple of times a week is plenty.

items.name: Roti (atta)
items.how: Not a protein food - listed so you can see why daal plus roti beats roti alone.

items.name: Doodh (full-fat)
items.how: One big glass is about 8 g, and it is the base for sattu and chana shakes.

items.name: Homemade paneer
items.how: Split doodh with lemon, then use the leftover paani in your atta.

items.name: Small / canned fish
items.how: Sardine-type fish: protein plus omega-3, still cheap.

items.name: Chicken (whole / leg quarters)
items.how: Buy whole or leg quarters instead of breast - same protein, lower price.
